title: Differential compatibility of degreewise signed Cech projection
statement: Let $X,M,r,W,D,e_p$ be a scheme, module sheaf, finite open family, nonnegative module-sheaf complex and all-tuple term identifications as in [def-pc-ordered-cech-module-coordinates]. Suppose $e$ intertwines each adjacent differential of $D$ with the Cech differential. Let $Q_p:D^p\to D^p$ be any family of module-sheaf maps satisfying the coordinate condition $c_{p,B,y}(Q_p s)=v_{p,B,y}(s)$ defined in [lem-pc-ordered-cech-degreewise-projection], for every degree, open, section and full tuple. Then for each $p\in\mathbb N$, $Q_p\circ d^p=d^p\circ Q_{p+1}$ in diagrammatic composition order. This asserts only differential compatibility of already supplied maps; it makes no existence claim and needs no local scalar compatibility assumption.

source.place: Tag 01FK, Lemma on ordered projection; Tag 01FM, the map cπ

proof.text: Construct, on each base open B, the intersection model S.W(p,t) = inf_k (W(lift(t(k))) intersect B). Its projection to the chosen product times B is an isomorphism: its projections give the reverse containment. Transport all tuple coordinates by coefficient restriction along this actual map. The transported coordinates determine a section, because evaluation preserves the tuple product, e is an isomorphism, and each restriction map is an isomorphism. These constructions and injectivity are proved private helpers in the assigned module.

Identify the finite filtered permutation sum with signedCechExtension. For an injective tuple, Tuple.unique_monotone shows that Tuple.sort is the only permutation passing the strict-increase filter; Finset.sum_eq_single reduces the sum to this term. For a repeated tuple no permutation passes the filter, since a strictly increasing reordered tuple is injective. Apply hQ, move coefficient restriction through the sum and integer multiples, and identify the two composites of restriction arrows by uniqueness in the poset of opens. Thus the transported Q is signed extension of ordered restriction.

Compose hd with each tuple projection and evaluate at B and a section. Use the already proved source-library theorem TopCat.Presheaf.cechComplexFunctor_d_π in WeilConjectures.Topology.Sheaves.CechComparison to expand the differential as the alternating face sum. Evaluation, composition and restriction preserve this finite sum and its integer multiples. For each face, the two coefficient restriction composites agree by uniqueness of arrows of opens. This proves the transported differential is S.differentialValue, without a new postponed statement.

Apply signedCechExtension_differential. Every face of an increasing tuple is increasing, since its index injection Fin.succAbove is strictly monotone. Apply signedCechExtension_increasing to each face to identify the ordered coordinates of the differential of a signed extension with those of the original cochain. Hence the transported differential commutes with the transported Q.

Apply Modules.hom_ext and section extensionality. Injectivity of the transported coordinates reduces the required equality to the proved projection-transport, differential-transport and signed-projection identities. All statements quantify over every base open and every degree. Empty index families give no tuples, and repeated tuples are included in the zero branch; no cover, nonemptiness or local scalar hypothesis was added.

theorem orderedCech_degreewise_projection_comm {X' : Scheme.{u}}
    (M : X'.Modules) {r : ℕ} (W₀ : ULift.{u} (Fin r) → X'.Opens)
    (D : CochainComplex X'.Modules ℕ)
    (e : ∀ p : ℕ, (PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).obj
          (D.X p).val ≅
        ((cechComplexFunctor W₀).obj
          ((prod.functor (C := X'.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
            (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj
              M.presheafModuleCat)).X p)
    (hd : ∀ p : ℕ,
        (PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).map
            (D.d p (p + 1)).val ≫ (e (p + 1)).hom =
          (e p).hom ≫ ((cechComplexFunctor W₀).obj
            ((prod.functor (C := X'.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
              (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj
              M.presheafModuleCat)).d p (p + 1))
    (Q : ∀ p : ℕ, D.X p ⟶ D.X p)
    (hQ : IsOrderedCechNaturalProjection M W₀ D e Q) (p : ℕ) :
    Q p ≫ D.d p (p + 1) = D.d p (p + 1) ≫ Q (p + 1)
